questions.question: The speed VS is defined as:
choices: speed for best specific range
design stress speed
safety speed for take-off in case of a contaminated runway
stalling speed or minimum steady flight speed at which the aeroplane is controllable
questions.answerText: stalling speed or minimum steady flight speed at which the aeroplane is controllable
questions.explanation: VS denotes the stalling or minimum steady controllable flight speed.

questions.question: Under what condition are pressure altitude and density altitude the same value?
choices: At standard temperature
When the altimeter setting is 1013 in. Hg
When the altimeter setting is 29.92 in. Hg
When indicated and pressure altitudes are the same value on the altimeter
questions.explanation: Density altitude equals pressure altitude at standard temperature.

questions.question: The climb gradient is defined as the ratio of:
choices: True airspeed to rate of climb
The increase of altitude to horizontal air distance expressed as a percentage
Rate of climb to true airspeed
The increase of altitude to distance over ground expressed as a percentage
questions.answerText: The increase of altitude to horizontal air distance expressed as a percentage
questions.explanation: Climb gradient is vertical height gained divided by horizontal distance.

questions.question: The absolute ceiling is defined as:
choices: The altitude where the maximum rate of climb is 0 ft/minute
The altitude where a certain maximum rate of climb (e.g. 100 ft/min) is attained
The outer boundary of our galaxy
The altitude where the rate of climb is maximum
questions.answerText: The altitude where the maximum rate of climb is 0 ft/minute
questions.explanation: At the absolute ceiling, maximum rate of climb is zero.

questions.question: Regarding take-off, the take-off decision speed V1:
choices: Is an airspeed at which the aeroplane is airborne but below 35 ft and the pilot has decided to continue or discontinue take-off
Is the airspeed on the ground at which the pilot is assumed to have made a decision to continue or discontinue take-off
Is the airspeed upon reaching 35 feet above the take-off surface
Is always equal to VEF (Engine Failure speed)
questions.answerText: Is the airspeed on the ground at which the pilot is assumed to have made a decision to continue or discontinue take-off
questions.explanation: V1 is the ground speed at which the take-off decision is made.

questions.question: The load factor in a turn in level flight with constant TAS depends on:
choices: the radius of the turn and the bank angle
the bank angle only
the true airspeed and the bank angle
the radius of the turn and the weight of the aeroplane
questions.explanation: In a coordinated level turn, load factor is determined by bank angle.

questions.question: The Density Altitude:
choices: is used to determine the aeroplane performance
is used to calculate the FL above the Transition Altitude
is used to establish minimum clearance of 2,000 feet over mountains
is equal to the pressure altitude
questions.answerText: is used to determine the aeroplane performance
questions.explanation: Density altitude is used to evaluate aircraft performance.

questions.question: The point where Drag coefficient/Lift coefficient is a minimum is:
choices: At stalling speed (VS)
The lowest point of the drag curve
The point where a tangent from the origin touches the drag curve
On the ‘back side’ of the drag curve
questions.answerText: The lowest point of the drag curve
questions.explanation: The minimum point of the drag curve is the keyed answer.

questions.question: For a piston-engine aircraft, the Critical Altitude is:
choices: The maximum altitude in standard atmosphere at which it is possible to maintain a specified power or manifold pressure
The maximum altitude at which it is possible to maintain a specified manifold pressure
The maximum altitude at which it is possible to maintain a specified power
The minimum altitude at which it is possible to maintain specified power or manifold pressure
questions.answerText: The maximum altitude in standard atmosphere at which it is possible to maintain a specified power or manifold pressure
questions.explanation: Critical altitude is the highest altitude at which specified power or manifold pressure can be maintained.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
choices: Landing distance on a grass runway is shorter than on tarmac because of the rougher surface
Deployment of lift dumpers will increase the effectiveness of the wheel brakes
A reduced flap setting for landing gives a shorter distance due to reduced lift and greater wheel load
Wheel braking is most effective when the wheels are locked
questions.answerText: Deployment of lift dumpers will increase the effectiveness of the wheel brakes
questions.explanation: Lift dumpers transfer more weight to the wheels and improve brake effectiveness.

questions.question: Decreasing take-off flap from 15° to 0° will probably result in a VLOF that is:
choices: unchanged
greatly reduced
reduced
increased
questions.explanation: With less flap-generated lift, a higher speed is needed for lift-off.

questions.question: The effect of a decrease in density is to:
choices: decrease take-off distance and increase rate of climb
increase take-off distance and reduce rate of climb
decrease take-off distance and reduce rate of climb
increase take-off distance and increase rate of climb
questions.answerText: increase take-off distance and reduce rate of climb
questions.explanation: Lower density reduces aircraft performance, increasing take-off distance and reducing climb rate.

questions.question: At the moment of lift-off:
choices: lift is greater than mass
rolling resistance is a maximum
lift and drag are equal to zero
lift is equal to weight
questions.explanation: At lift-off, lift balances aircraft weight.

questions.question: An upward runway slope:
choices: increases the available take-off distance
increases the available rate of climb
increases the take-off distance required
decreases the take-off distance required
questions.explanation: An uphill slope opposes acceleration and increases required take-off distance.

questions.question: Which combination produces the best take-off performance in a normal atmosphere?
choices: Low altitude, high ambient temperature
High altitude, high ambient temperature
High altitude, low ambient temperature
Low altitude, low ambient temperature
questions.explanation: Low altitude and low temperature give denser air and better performance.

questions.question: What is the effect of an increased flap angle on the optimum lift-to-drag ratio?
choices: The optimum ratio decreases initially, then increases at higher flap settings
None
The optimum ratio will decrease
The optimum ratio will increase
questions.explanation: Increased flap adds drag and reduces optimum L/D.

questions.question: The effect of increased weight on a glide descent in a normal atmosphere is: forward speed ___, rate of descent ___.
choices: decreased, rate decreases
increased, rate decreases
decreased, rate increases
increased, rate increases
questions.explanation: At the same glide angle, more weight requires greater speed and yields a greater descent rate.

questions.question: The forces acting on an aircraft during the take-off run are:
choices: weight, thrust and drag
lift, weight, aerodynamic drag, thrust and mechanical friction
lift, weight, aerodynamic drag and thrust
lift, weight and aerodynamic drag
questions.answerText: lift, weight, aerodynamic drag, thrust and mechanical friction
questions.explanation: The take-off run includes lift, weight, thrust, aerodynamic drag, and mechanical friction.

questions.question: Landing distance will be increased as a result of all the following:
choices: increased temperature, increased pressure altitude, downhill runway slope
increased temperature, decreased pressure altitude, downhill runway slope
decreased temperature, decreased pressure altitude, uphill runway slope
increased temperature, increased pressure altitude, uphill runway slope
questions.answerText: increased temperature, increased pressure altitude, downhill runway slope
questions.explanation: Hotter air, higher pressure altitude, and downhill slope increase landing distance.

questions.question: Descending at a constant IAS and constant gradient of descent, the pitch angle must be:
choices: increased rapidly
kept constant
progressively increased
progressively decreased
questions.explanation: As the aircraft descends at constant IAS and gradient, pitch progressively decreases.

questions.question: Which airspeed provides the greatest gain in altitude in the shortest distance during climb after take-off?
choices: VA
VY
VX
V2
questions.explanation: VX maximizes climb gradient and height gained per distance.

questions.question: Which statement about the lift/drag ratio in straight and level flight is correct?
choices: The highest value is reached when lift equals aircraft weight
At the highest value of lift/drag ratio, total drag is lowest
The ratio always increases as lift decreases
The highest value is reached when lift is zero
questions.answerText: At the highest value of lift/drag ratio, total drag is lowest
questions.explanation: At maximum L/D, total drag is at its minimum.

questions.question: If aircraft weight is increased, the maximum lift/drag ratio will:
choices: increase although the aircraft will have to be flown more slowly
not be affected
increase
decrease
questions.explanation: Maximum L/D is determined by the aircraft drag polar, not aircraft weight.

questions.question: Skin friction due to air viscosity along the wing surface is part of:
choices: interference drag
form drag
parasite drag
induced drag
questions.explanation: Skin-friction drag is a component of parasite drag.

questions.question: What phenomenon causes induced drag?
choices: The increased pressure at the leading edge
Wing tanks
The spanwise flow inward below the wing and outward above the wing
Wingtip vortices
questions.explanation: Wingtip vortices and their downwash produce induced drag.

questions.question: Maintaining thickness/chord ratio but changing to a supercritical wing section will:
choices: reduce the aft shift of CP in the transonic range
lead to more prominent shockwave formation
make lateral stability more critical
give the aircraft an increased range
questions.answerText: give the aircraft an increased range
questions.explanation: A supercritical wing reduces wave drag and can improve range.

questions.question: Flying at the maximum rate of climb speed (Vy) you will obtain maximum:
choices: altitude at maximum boost setting
altitude in the shortest distance and time
altitude in the shortest time
altitude in the shortest distance
questions.explanation: Vy is the speed for maximum rate of climb, so it gains altitude in the shortest time.

questions.question: Find the maximum rate of climb for an airplane weighing 19,815 lb when PR = 1,884 hp and PA = 6,636 hp.
questions.explanation: Using excess power to calculate vertical speed gives about 7,914 ft/min.

questions.question: What is the CD for an airplane with the following characteristics? Wingspan 53.3 ft; wing area 318 ft?; normal gross weight 19,815 lb; fuel capacity 1,119 gal of kerosene; two turbofan engines of 3,650-lb thrust each at sea level; specific fuel consumption 0.6 lb fuel/(lb thrust)(h); parasite drag coefficient CD,0 = 0.02; Oswald efficiency factor e = 0.81.
questions.explanation: The total drag coefficient is the sum of parasite and induced contributions for the stated aircraft condition; the keyed result is 0.022.

questions.question: What is the relationship between CD,0 and CD,i at minimum power required?
choices: CD,0 = CD,i
CD,0 = 1/3 CD,i
1/3 CD,0 = CD,i
Varies with angle of attack
questions.explanation: At minimum power required, induced drag coefficient is three times parasite drag coefficient.
